summary.name: International Typographic Style (Swiss Style)
summary.visualIdentity: A supplemental design reference, not a directly named style in the source collection. Uses a column grid, baseline alignment, repeated spacing, asymmetric composition, and generous negative space. Left-aligned sans-serif type carries a clear size hierarchy, with black and white dominant, restrained accent color, and grid-aligned photography. Elements animate along layout axes and settle on shared alignment points without disrupting reading order.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly suited to posters, identity work, and typographic statements where grid and type carry the message. Good fit for UI and product storytelling, editorial and minimalist layouts, and motion posters or staged geometric compositions. Hybrids with chart or kinetic-type styles are suggested only when data must be explained or headlines must perform.
summary.limitations: Adapt or omit when recomposition changes hierarchy without explaining the subject, when anchored subjects crop key details or push text into unsafe areas, or when pinning disrupts layout. Charts must stay in black, white, and the single red accent. Decorative chart animation without a stated value is to be avoided. Source does not specify further limitations.
summary.palette: Suggested, not approved: black and white with one restrained red accent. Tokens: background #FFFFFF (layout role), foreground #000000, accent_1 #D32F2F. No gradients enabled; use discrete base tokens only. Task-supplied exact colors override these and must not be altered. Contrast: foreground on background 21:1; accent_1 with background text 4.979:1. Two-color checks only; verify actual composited frames, and never recolor assets to improve contrast.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion moves along horizontal or vertical layout axes and settles on grid lines, with no springs or overshoot. Reading order must never change mid-animation. Smooth authored easing suits this style, but sharp cuts and reading holds are preserved where deliberate. Video is driven entirely by seekable composition time. Interactive delivery may use scroll, hover, or keyboard input, with reduced-motion fallback to a static layout. Optional motion references (motion-007, -012, -013, -015) apply only when their defining action fits the scene.
summary.audio: Source gives no fixed audio requirement; the style does not mandate any audio layer or genre. Audio direction is a task-specific suggestion, to be proposed from topic, audience, and motion cadence. Speech must remain intelligible, so music or effects must leave space for narration. Audio must be sourced or created as authorized assets. Picture and sound are synchronized and verified in the final video.
summary.assetRequirements: Requires loaded local fonts for sans-serif typography and grid-aligned photography or SVG geometry aligned to the baseline grid. Source does not specify exact asset formats or quantities. Any missing assets must be stated. Optional chart work uses bundled Chartist with local CSS, or native SVG. Optional motion-reference assets, such as tldraw exports, must keep editable layers separate when needed.
summary.combinations: Use Swiss Style alone for posters, identity, and typographic statements. Hybrid with style-097 (diagram and chart layer inside the column grid) for research summaries or explainers with verified figures; red marks only the one value discussed. Hybrid with style-093 (kinetic headline motion) for title sequences or manifestos; one sans family, one red element per frame, and no overshoot. Avoid multi-hue categorical palettes, centered or rotated chart labels, and script or display faces.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition, timing, audio sync, validation, and export. Remotion is only a conditional fallback, when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation applies, and the reason must be recorded. HTML/CSS Grid and SVG act as the style renderer. GSAP is the paused, seekable motion engine, with Motion optional. chroma.js validates colors. Choose one owner per animated property. Verify seeks, decoded frames, and audio sync before delivery.
